thread:
sara_ops: paging oncall — TidalPay is getting sustained 429s from their dedicated pool since 09:12 UTC. Customer reports spike in auth requests and mobile retries. seeing 100% queue saturation on pool-ded-42 :warning:
incident-bot: ALERT: high-429-rate detected on pool-ded-42 (tenant: tidalpay). Severity: P1. Pager duty routed to eli_oncall. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/pool-ded-42/1749998881
eli_oncall: looking. pulling metrics now. can someone drop the pool qps and check the fairshare counters?
maria_reliability: from metrics — average qps from TidalPay jumped x12 at 09:11, 95th latency still fine but queue depth spiked. KV cache hits unchanged. Likely client retry storm.
eli_oncall: ok rate limiting is kicking in but ephemeral queue overflow => redispatch causing synthetic 429s. I can temporarily increase tenant socket limit on that pool but need signoff — that will reduce headroom for other tenants.
vinny_sales: pinging Jordan (AE) — customer is on enterprise contract with burst allowances but requires ops authorization for manual override. Jordan: can you confirm authorization?
jordan_account: on it. customer asking for a 30s emergency burst lift to stabilize UX. legal said ok for short window if we document. I can approve up to 2x of committed qps for 10 minutes.
eli_oncall: 2x for 10m should be fine. I'll enact emergency lift and monitor. steps: 1) apply temporary throttle override for tenant tidalpay on pool-ded-42 2) enable per-tenant backoff header to mobile 3) route non-critical background jobs to fallback pool-ded-43 4) keep canary traffic at 5%
maria_reliability: runbook notes — apply with `./opsctl pool override --pool pool-ded-42 --tenant tidalpay --qps-multiplier 2 --duration 600` then `curl -X POST https://internal-api/tenants/tidalpay/flags -d '{"backoff_header":true}'`
eli_oncall: executing now (will confirm).
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK ACTION: override command accepted. Change request ID cr-20260315-42. Audit trail: https://audit.redwood.internal/cr-20260315-42
eli_oncall: override applied. showing reduced enqueue rate and backlog starting to drain. latency stable.
sara_ops: can we also divert their heavy batch sync traffic? looks like 2 endpoints hitting in parallel.
maria_reliability: blocking rule created to route `/sync/bulk` to pool-ded-43 with weight 0.2 for 10m. applied.
vinny_sales: customer says they can flip client-side retry to exponential backoff immediately — will coordinate.
jordan_account: confirmed authorization in thread, will follow up with legal doc. also cc billing to note emergency lift.
eli_oncall: backlog at 30% now. continuing to monitor. setting alert to watch for negative impact on other tenants — currently within fairshare headroom.
incident-bot: NOTE: oncall changed — eli_oncall -> maria_reliability at 09:25 UTC per rotation. Handoff: summary of current state and actions posted.
maria_reliability: taking over. confirming replication to fallback pool succeeded and no cross-tenant traffic leak.
sara_ops: heads up — if backlog doesn't reach zero in 8m we escalate to infra to add short-lived burst nodes, that will require infra approval (lead time ~5m).
eli_oncall: leaving logs and commands in thread before stepping off. `kubectl get pods -n redwood-pool-ded-42 --selector=pool=ded-42` showed 12/12 ready. No OOMs.
eli_oncall: final: override will auto-revoke at 10:21 UTC. If we need extension, require Jordan + ops lead signoff. passing to maria for follow-up. :raised_hands:
maria_reliability: monitoring 5m. backlog drained to 5% at 09:28. dropping temporary diversion at 09:35. will confirm post-mortem owner.
sara_ops: creating incident ticket and assigning to maria for RCA. please include client retry pattern, pool sizing, and a clearer emergency lift runbook for AE approvals.
jordan_account: I'll notify customer of the temporary lift and ask them to patch retry logic tonight. thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (P1 -> P2) at 09:40 UTC. Final note: emergency override auto-revoked. Postmortem ticket: INC-2026-0315-42 assigned to maria_reliability.
maria_reliability: acknowledging. I'll open the postmortem doc and link metrics + sample request traces.
